_readme: Traditional RP isolated phonemes - HUMAN recordings, one consistent
reference voice. This manifest is production tooling only; it never ships
(tools/ is excluded from the deployed artifact). It is also the file
tools/prep_phonemes.py reads to know the order and the names, so a session
cannot be prepped without it.
Workflow: record each entry -> name the file <slug>.mp3 -> run
python3 tools/prep_phonemes.py <folder> --manifest tools/phoneme_manifest_rp.json --out prepped/
python3 tools/import_phonemes.py prepped/ --dialect rp --voice reference --dry-run
then again without --dry-run, listen at #audit, mark Good, export the
flags file and commit it. Nothing plays for a learner until the exact
dialect/voice/slug id is in APPROVED_PHONEMES.
General guidance: quiet room, consistent mic distance, no added vowel
after consonants, no trailing breath. A syllable demonstration must
sound like a syllable ON PURPOSE - it is labelled as one in the app.
Entry order follows docs/PHONEME_RECORDING_LIST.md, because
tools/prep_phonemes.py --split names files BY THIS ORDER when it cuts one
continuous take - recording in a different order misnames every clip.
Syllable-demo frame: /ɑː/ (PALM/BATH) - frames written /ɑːpɑː/, /ɑːtɑː/
and so on. It is this accent's own long open back unrounded vowel, present
in the entries file (palm_bath_vowel) and given to RP by the spec's BATH
split; being open and unrounded it masks nothing about the consonant's
closure, release or voicing, and it is the nearest RP counterpart to the
nam manifest's /ɑ/ frame.
Cast a trained stage or period-drama speaker with a conservative, Gimson-
era RP - a classical theatre voice, not a contemporary British screen
voice. Measured, evenly weighted stresses, the precision carrying the
accent.
Biggest booth risk: modern Standard British leaking in. Listen for SQUARE
flattening to a steady /ɛː/, any /t/ going to [ʔ], a fused yod in tune,
tensed happY /i/, or a fronted GOOSE [ʉː]. Any of those is a retake, not a
note.
Second risk: rhoticity. NURSE, PALM/BATH, THOUGHT and the three centring
diphthongs must end with no r-colour at all - a speaker who also works
American will colour them without hearing it.
Ask the speaker not to perform 'plumminess'. The spec flags the marked
upper-class varieties as variable, not the target; the reference clips
must stay the neutral conservative centre.
SHARE RULE. Most of these sounds are the same in every course, so one take
is recorded and copied into each. That is NOT safe for every entry: where an
accent's own published spec names a departure, that accent records its own.
Each entry carries "take": "shared" or "accent-specific" - never reuse
another course's file for an accent-specific one.

entries.guidance: Controlled voiceless sustain /fff/, ~1s, airflow steady. No vowel before or after.
Voiced sustain /vvv/, ~1s, buzz audible throughout. No added vowel.
Voiceless dental sustain /θθθ/, ~1s, tongue tip at the teeth and airflow steady. No vowel before or after.
Voiced dental sustain /ððð/, ~1s, tongue tip at the teeth with voicing on throughout. No added vowel.
Controlled voiceless sustain /sss/, ~1s. No vowel before or after.
Voiced sustain /zzz/, ~1s, buzz audible throughout. No added vowel.
Voiceless postalveolar sustain /ʃʃʃ/, ~1s, lips lightly rounded and airflow steady. No vowel before or after.
Voiced sustain /ʒʒʒ/, ~1s - the middle of measure, buzzing throughout. No added vowel.
Clean voiceless /h/, ~1s of audible breath at steady pressure. Breath only - no vowel before or after.
Hummed /mmm/, ~1s, lips closed the whole time. No vowel before or after.
Sustained /nnn/, ~1s, tongue tip on the alveolar ridge throughout. No vowel before or after.
Sustained velar nasal /ŋ/, ~1s, back of the tongue held up. No vowel before or after, and no /g/ release at the end.
Sustained /l/, ~1s, tongue tip on the ridge. Record the clear [l] of pre-vocalic position, not the dark [ɫ] of feel. No added vowel.
Sustained /r/, ~1s, as the postalveolar approximant [ɹ] - no tap and no trill, no vowel before or after. In RP this sounds only before a vowel.
Steady /ɪ/ as in kit, ~0.7-1s at stable pitch. Keep it lax - no drift toward /iː/; this is also the lax vowel RP ends happy on.
Steady /e/ as in dress, ~0.7-1s. Keep it a monophthong - no FACE glide, and clearly closer than the near-open TRAP /æ/.
Steady /æ/ as in trap, ~0.7-1s. Hold the traditional RP height - do not lower it toward the open Standard British [a].
entries.takeNote: Standard British records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Stressed /ʌ/ as in but, ~0.7-1s. Fuller than schwa and clearly separate from it. No added length, no glide.
Short rounded /ʊ/ as in foot, ~0.7-1s. Lax with light rounding - do not tense or lengthen it toward /uː/.
Short rounded /ɒ/ as in lot, ~0.7s. Open and only lightly rounded - lower than THOUGHT /ɔː/, never the unrounded American /ɑ/.
Neutral unstressed schwa, short side of ~0.7s, low energy - the colourless 'uh'. No r-colour: RP is non-rhotic.
Tense long /iː/ as in fleece, ~1s, steady - resist any onglide. Full length: RP keeps happy lax /ɪ/, so this is the long vowel only.
entries.takeNote: General Australian records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Long open back /ɑː/ as in palm - and in bath, dance, grass, ask, under the RP BATH split. ~1s, steady, unrounded, no r-colour.
Long /ɔː/ as in thought, ~1s: open-mid and closely rounded throughout, clearly higher than LOT /ɒ/. Non-rhotic - north takes no r.
Back rounded /uː/ as in goose, ~1s, rounding steady. Keep it back - no fronting toward the Standard British [ʉː].
entries.takeNote: Standard British records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Long open-mid central /ɜː/ as in nurse, ~1s, even and stressed - fuller and lower than schwa, not a stretched schwa. No r-colour at all.
Complete glide /eɪ/ as in face, ~1s: start at mid front /e/ and land near /ɪ/. The journey must be audible - no monophthong.
entries.takeNote: Cockney records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Complete audible glide /aɪ/ as in price, ~1s - start open, land near /ɪ/. The whole journey, evenly measured, no clipped landing.
entries.takeNote: Cockney records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Complete glide /ɔɪ/ as in choice, ~1s: start back and rounded, land near /ɪ/. Let the rounding go as you travel.
Complete glide /əʊ/ as in goat, ~1s: start on central unrounded schwa, then round the lips into a close back finish. Not the American /oʊ/.
entries.takeNote: Cockney records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Complete glide /aʊ/ as in mouth, ~1s: start open, finish rounded and close back. Both ends audible, no monophthong.
entries.takeNote: Cockney records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Full centring glide /ɪə/ as in near, ~1s: /ɪ/ to schwa, both targets reached. No smoothing to a long [ɪː], and no r at the end.
entries.takeNote: Standard British records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Full centring glide /eə/ as in square, ~1s: a real journey from mid front /e/ to schwa. The steady /ɛː/ monophthong is Standard British - not this.
Full centring glide /ʊə/ as in cure, ~1s: /ʊ/ to schwa. Record the conservative diphthong, not the later-RP merger toward /ɔː/.
entries.takeNote: General Australian records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Syllable demo (stops and affricates cannot be sustained): a clean /ɑːpɑː/ - full closure and a crisp aspirated release, never a standalone 'puh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːbɑː/ - voicing running through the closure and a gentle release. No aspiration, no standalone 'buh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːtɑː/ - a careful, fully articulated alveolar /t/ with a crisply aspirated release. No glottal [ʔ], no tap. Never 'tuh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːdɑː/ - a true voiced alveolar /d/, fully articulated and never tapped. No 'duh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːkɑː/ - clean velar closure and a crisply aspirated release. No 'kuh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːgɑː/ - voiced velar closure and release, voicing audible through it. No aspiration, no 'guh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːtʃɑː/ - stop and fricative fused into one affricate, not /t/ plus /ʃ/. Never 'chuh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːdʒɑː/ - one voiced affricate with voicing through it, not /d/ plus /ʒ/. No 'juh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːwɑː/ - a rounded labial-velar glide travelling through, lips rounded at the start. No 'wuh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːjɑː/ - a clean palatal glide. RP retains its yods (tune /tjuːn/), so keep /j/ separate and never fused to /tʃ/. No 'yuh'.
